included_prs.title: fix(docusign): Connect listener provisioning — add required deliveryMode SIM
included_prs.ci_summary: Required checks green on exact head SHA (verify at merge time).
included_prs.rollback_note: Revert PR; restores prior docusign.ts parse chain (no data.envelopeSummary nesting, no deliveryMode SIM) and the prior deploy-worker.yml docusign_connect_hmac_secret binding.
included_prs.soak_coverage: THREE changed surfaces, three coverage postures. (1) REST v2.1 SIM payload parse (parseDocusignConnectPayload data.envelopeSummary nesting) — EXERCISED end-to-end on the rig against the changed code (git_sha 55551e46): a signed nested REST v2.1 completed-envelope POST returned HTTP 200 {ok:true,orphaned:true} and logged 'DocuSign webhook: unknown connected account' accountId=acct-rc2-signed (parse reached the integration-lookup + HMAC-verify stage); the SAME nested payload UNSIGNED returned HTTP 401 invalid_signature with NO 'malformed body' log (parse succeeded — the pre-#1690 chain would have thrown 'not a completed envelope event'); a garbage control payload returned HTTP 401 + 'malformed body' log (parse-failure control). See webhook_liveness_evidence. (2) provisionConnectListener deliveryMode 'SIM' + eventData restv2.1 (buildArkovaConnectConfig / buildConnectPayload) — NOT exercised live on the rig: provisioning would create a real DocuSign Connect listener on the production DocuSign account pointing at the rig URL, which is prohibited on a soak rig (see deviations). Covered by the PR's own unit tests (docusign.test.ts asserts body.deliveryMode==='SIM' and body.eventData==={format:'json',version:'restv2.1'}) + worker boots cleanly with the provisioning module present. Real end-to-end provisioning proof is the documented post-merge prod residual. (3) deploy-worker.yml DOCUSIGN_CONNECT_HMAC_SECRET -> docusign_connect_hmac_secret_prod durable binding — CI/deploy-config only (one line in .github/workflows/deploy-worker.yml). NOT bound on this rig with the prod secret; an INERT placeholder DOCUSIGN_CONNECT_HMAC_SECRET was used to satisfy config Zod and drive the HMAC-verify path. Coverage = the deploy-worker.yml diff + CI; prod cutover proves the live binding.

webhook_liveness_evidence.note: Changed-path (#1690) liveness for POST /webhooks/docusign, driven WITHOUT any real DocuSign secret or API call. ENABLE_DOCUSIGN_WEBHOOK=true mounts the route; an INERT DOCUSIGN_CONNECT_HMAC_SECRET (random, NOT the prod secret) drives the HMAC-verify path. ENABLE_DOCUSIGN_OAUTH is OFF and DOCUSIGN_INTEGRATION_KEY/DOCUSIGN_CLIENT_SECRET are both UNSET, so the OAuth/provisionConnectListener flow is unreachable — the rig can never call or provision against the real DocuSign account.

deviations: PROFILE = mock (USE_MOCKS=true / anchoring off / network=signet), matching the canonical shared-staging T2 posture and RC-1 (rc-t2-worker-batch-20260726). Rationale: none of #1690's changed lines touch services/worker/src/chain/, the broadcast path, or RPC; mock exercises 100% of the reachable changed lines (the DocuSign webhook parse path is fully exercised, see webhook_liveness_evidence).

NO real DocuSign secret bound and NO real DocuSign API/provisioning call made from the rig. ENABLE_DOCUSIGN_OAUTH is OFF; DOCUSIGN_INTEGRATION_KEY and DOCUSIGN_CLIENT_SECRET are both UNSET (config.ts pair-rule satisfied: both unset); DOCUSIGN_CONNECT_HMAC_SECRET is an INERT random placeholder (verifies inbound signatures only, never calls out). This is deliberate: a rig-side provisionConnectListener run would create a DocuSign Connect listener on the PRODUCTION DocuSign account pointing at the rig URL. The real deliveryMode-SIM provisioning proof is the post-merge prod residual (documented in included_prs[0].soak_coverage surface 2).

Supabase project created via `supabase projects create` (CLI, controlled DB password) instead of MCP create_project, because clean_mirror requires numeric-ledger schema replay via `supabase db push --linked` which needs a known DB password (MCP create_project does not expose one). Cost (~$10/mo micro) acknowledged; tear down after soak matures + merges.

Deployed via `gcloud run deploy` on the digest-pinned RC image (sha256:a66752b7...) rather than scripts/staging/deploy.sh, because deploy.sh is hard-scoped to the shared arkova-worker-staging service and cannot target an ad-hoc isolated service.

provision-isolated-rig.sh (the documented orchestrator) was NOT used to --apply: its mock profile deploys at min-instances=0 with no Cloud Scheduler (unsuitable for a T2 cron-driven soak), and its defaults are hardwired for a single-PR T3 chain soak. Standup was done manually to match T2 semantics + wire the 3 changed-path-neighbor cron routes + the DocuSign webhook route.

Soak clock set at rev 00002 (not 00001): rev 00001 booted with an empty switchboard_flags table (env fallback => ENABLE_BATCH_ANCHORING off); the flag was seeded to the DB and the worker restarted (gcloud run services update BATCH_ANCHORING_FLAG_LOADED=1) so flagRegistry.init() re-read it (source=db). Same image digest; RC head unchanged. The restart happened BEFORE the clock started, so this is a clean clock anchor, not a mid-soak reset.

SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET is an inert 64-hex value (>=32 chars), not the project's real JWT secret (not cleanly exposed by the Management API). Functionally sufficient: this mock rig verifies no user JWTs during the cron/webhook lifecycle; the value only needs to satisfy config.ts Zod. Boot-critical STRIPE_*/API_KEY_HMAC/CRON secrets reuse the shared `-staging` Secret Manager secrets.
